title: Bunt popped up and caught by the pitcher, runner holds: a fly out, not a sacrifice

expect.line: b1 popped out bunting to P.
expect.note: A bunt in the air is airborne — caught, it retires the batter like any pop-up, and the runner owes a retouch rather than a force. It is still a bunt: had the runner moved up, the sacrifice question would be the bunt's. Nobody moved, so there is nothing to ask and nothing derives. The pitch carries no batterAction: the trajectory says she bunted, whichever surface said it first.
